text:
The query is already simple and the plan is reasonable: a bitmap index scan on `tenant_id` followed by a filter, in about 10 ms for roughly 23k rows. A query rewrite has no real lever here. A real gain would need a dedicated index such as `(tenant_id, created_at)`, but indexes are not allowed. I am therefore returning the original query unchanged.

```sql
-- name: revenue_orders
-- owner: finance
-- params: tenant_id, from, to
-- Revenue-bearing orders in a window. Period grouping (day/week/month, week
-- start, fiscal month boundaries) is applied by the service layer so the same
-- query feeds every grouping the dashboard offers.
SELECT o.id,
       o.created_at,
       o.status,
       o.total_cents,
       o.currency
  FROM orders o
 WHERE o.tenant_id = %(tenant_id)s
   AND o.created_at >= %(from)s
   AND o.created_at <  %(to)s
   AND o.status IN ('paid', 'processing', 'shipped', 'delivered')
```

The plan already uses the best available access path for this predicate. Rewriting with CTEs or splitting up the conditions would not speed it up and could actually make the plan worse.
